title: Will an EU state restrict farmland purchases by non-EU sovereign funds by 2028?

masked.note: Commodity names and calendar dates are hidden; months are relative to now (t0) and prices are an index, 100 at t-12.

forecasts.name: Land-Grab Realist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Public outrage over Gulf sovereign wealth funds buying up Eastern and Southern European arable acreage will force protectionist legislative bans across EU states.

forecasts.name: Climate Pessimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: As arable land contracts under climatic desertification, member states will treat sovereign farmland grabs as existential threats to food sovereignty.

forecasts.name: Geopolitics Hawk · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Food sovereignty is national defense. Escalating global conflict will spur European governments to block foreign sovereign asset grabs.

forecasts.name: Copa-Cogeca (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Food sovereignty and protecting family farms demand strict safeguards against foreign sovereign funds purchasing vital European farmland.

forecasts.name: IMF (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Rising trade policy friction and strategic autonomy imperatives increase incentives for EU states to protect critical agricultural assets.

forecasts.name: BirdLife Europe, EEB, WWF and Greenpeace (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Concerns over food sovereignty, rural depopulation, and land stewardship make restrictions on non-EU sovereign acquisitions increasingly probable.

forecasts.name: IFPRI (Joseph Glauber) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Mounting geopolitical tensions and rising agricultural protectionism will incentivize at least one EU government to restrict strategic land purchases.

forecasts.name: European Commission DG AGRI (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Geopolitical conflict and heightened focus on EU strategic autonomy and food security bolster farmland purchase scrutiny.

forecasts.name: Macro / Dollar · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Shifting global liquidity and sovereign fund capital flows into real assets frequently trigger national protectionist backlash.

forecasts.name: Agronomist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Heightened concerns over food sovereignty and climate stress on arable land favor stricter European regulatory fences on strategic non-EU sovereign acquisitions.

forecasts.name: FAO (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Food security concerns and rising foreign control of arable acreage push EU member states toward protective land ownership regulations.

forecasts.name: Scott Irwin (farmdoc) (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Trade and investment restrictions are a persistent political risk. Pressures on domestic farm sovereignty keep odds near even.

forecasts.name: Crowd Follower · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: The market sits at 52%. Following consensus closely is the best course given balanced political trends.

forecasts.name: USDA WASDE (narrative) · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: Strategic asset scrutiny in EU agriculture is rising steadily, making targeted farmland ownership restrictions a coin-flip policy outcome by 2028.

forecasts.name: Adaptation Optimist · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: EU states need private and institutional capital to finance agronomic adaptation, limiting appetite for outright bans.

forecasts.name: Efficient-Market Skeptic · Phi-4
forecasts.rationale: EU legislative processes are slow and diluted by compromise. Nationalist protectionist rhetoric rarely yields outright sovereign fund land bans.
